hypothesis: Registered frequency counting is a sufficient estimator of concern at door 3's bound: on three registered literal 24-draw task sequences, the plug-in choice (kappa_concern of the empirical frequencies) equals the oracle choice for all prefixes n >= a registered minimal step (seq_bag 1, seq_mix 2, seq_pair 6), and the misspecification control (holding seq_mix's screen under seq_pair's true concern) costs exactly 4 more than the oracle screen.

controls.description: The three draw sequences are literal registered tuples; nothing is sampled at run time and there is no RNG.
The estimator is empirical frequency counting, written before the run; no SGD, no tuning, no learned representations.
All plug-in weights, expected costs, and gaps are Fractions; no floats.
Each sequence's oracle concern must reproduce door 3's banked choice (q_perm / q_stab0 / q_id) through the unchanged menu and cost rule.
estimation_works, estimation_fails, and inconclusive are all valid passing runs.

gates.criterion: Estimator, sequences, oracle anchors, convergence steps, and verdict rule specified before the run.
Exactly three registered literal sequences of 24 draws each.
Plug-in weights and misspecification numbers serialize as exact integers or fractions.
Oracle concerns reproduce door 3's banked choices q_perm / q_stab0 / q_id.
The full 24-row choice trace per sequence and the observed minimal steps are recorded.
The misspecification control (q_stab0 vs q_id under seq_pair's true concern) is recorded with exact costs.
Verdict is estimation_works, estimation_fails, or inconclusive.
No valence, no learning beyond registered counting, no LLM, no new master object.
